item.title: Why Keep Kosher? The Reasons Behind Kashrut | Kashrut Course, Part 1
item.description:
Why keep kosher? The Torah explains only two of its food laws, so the reasons offered are tastes: health or character for forbidden animals, several explanations of meat and milk and of terefah, and the four things kashrut gives as a whole, from self-discipline to national identity.

item.title: Should a Jew Be Vegan? The Torah on Eating Meat | Kashrut Course, Part 2
item.description:
Does the Torah share the vegan philosophy of avoiding all exploitation of animals? The obvious starting point is that eating meat is accepted, with korbanot, festival meat and Shabbat delicacies, but the misvah of covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal suggests it is not so simple.

item.title: Why Wait Six Hours? Milk and Meat Halachot | Kashrut Course, Part 3
item.description:
Meat and milk before Shavuot: the three Torah prohibitions of eating, cooking and benefit, why poultry is only rabbinic, microwave cooking, how long to wait after meat and who may wait less, bread from a meaty oven, and the reasons for eating dairy on Shavuot.

item.title: Does It Need the Mikveh? Immersing New Utensils | Kashrut Course, Part 4
item.description:
Which new utensils need immersion in a mikveh, and with a berakhah? Tevilat Kelim as a Torah misvah separate from kashering, the rules for metal, glass, plastic and other materials, items bought from non-Jews, electrical appliances, eating at a non-religious host, and a convert's own utensils.

item.title: Cooked by a Non-Jew? Bishul Akum and Pat Akum | Kashrut Course, Part 5
item.description:
Does food need a hekhsher to be kosher? The reasons behind Bishul Akum, which foods it covers and which it does not, what a Jew must do in the kitchen, eating in restaurants, and when bakery bread, cereals, biscuits and crackers may be bought.

item.title: Glatt, Halak or Just Kosher? Meat, Milk and Cheese | Kashrut Course, Part 6
item.description:
